tr.text: Om. The yonder sun indeed is the honey of the gods. Of this honey, heaven is the cross-beam, the sky is the honey comb, and (the water particles in) the rays are the eggs.

sa: तस्य ये प्राञ्चो रश्मयस् ता एवास्य प्राच्यो मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: tasya ye prāñco raśmayas tā evāsya prācyo madhunāḍyaḥ ।
words: a flower; blossom; the menstrual flux

tr.text: The eastern rays of that sun are its eastern honey-cells; the Riks are the bees, (the ritual of) the Rig-Veda is the flower and those waters are the nectar. Those very Riks (the bees) pressed this RigVeda. From it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour (of limbs), (alertness of) the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
iast: tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso ’jāyata ॥

tr.text: The eastern rays of that sun are its eastern honey-cells; the Riks are the bees, (the ritual of) the Rig-Veda is the flower and those waters are the nectar. Those very Riks (the bees) pressed this RigVeda. From it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour (of limbs), (alertness of) the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य रोहितं रूपम् ॥
iast: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya rohitaṃ rūpam ॥
words: to flow away or into; to trickle through

tr.text: That juice flowed forth; it settled by the side of the sun. Verily, this it is that appears as the red hue of the sun.

sa: अथ ये ऽस्य दक्षिणा रश्मयस् ता एवास्य दक्षिणा मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: atha ye ’sya dakṣiṇā raśmayas tā evāsya dakṣiṇā madhunāḍyaḥ ।
words: a flower; blossom; the menstrual flux

tr.text: And its southern rays are its southern honey cells. The Yajus verses are the bees. The YajurVeda is the flower; and those waters are the nectar.

sa: तानि वा एतानि यजूंष्य् एतं यजुर्वेदम् अभ्यतपन् ।
तस्य अभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
iast: tāni vā etāni yajūṃṣy etaṃ yajurvedam abhyatapan ।
tasya abhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso ’jāyata ॥

tr.text: Those very Yajus verses pressed this Yajur-Veda. And from it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour of limbs, alertness of the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य शुक्लं रूपम् ॥
iast: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya śuklaṃ rūpam ॥
words: to flow away or into; to trickle through

tr.text: It, flowed forth; it settled by the side of the sun. Verily, this it is that appears as the white hue of the sun.

sa: अथ ये ऽस्य प्रत्यञ्चो रश्मायस् ता एवास्य प्रतीच्यो मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: atha ye ’sya pratyañco raśmāyas tā evāsya pratīcyo madhunāḍyaḥ ।
words: a flower; blossom; the menstrual flux

tr.text: And its western rays are its western honey cells. The Samans are the bees. The Sama-Veda is the flower; and those waters are the nectar.

sa: तानि वा एतानि सामान्य् एतं सामवेदम् अभ्यतपन् ।
तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
iast: tāni vā etāni sāmāny etaṃ sāmavedam abhyatapan ।
tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso ’jāyata ॥
words: name of one of the three principal Vedas
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
the sap or juice of plants

tr.text: Those very Samans pressed this Sama-Veda. From it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour of limbs, alertness of the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य कृष्णं रूपम् ॥
iast: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya kṛṣṇaṃ rūpam ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: It flowed forth; it settled by the side of the sun. Verily, this it is that appears as the black hue of the sun.

sa: अथ ये ऽस्योदञ्चो रश्मयस् ता एवास्योदीच्यो मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: atha ye ’syodañco raśmayas tā evāsyodīcyo madhunāḍyaḥ ।
words: being or living in the north
a priest who has to do with fire and Soma

tr.text: And its northern rays are its northern honey cells. The Mantras of the Atharva-Veda are the bees. The Itihasa and the Purana are the flower; and those waters are the nectar.

sa: ते वा एते ऽथर्वाङ्गिरस एतद् इतिहासपूराणम् अभ्यतपन् ।
तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियां वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
iast: te vā ete ’tharvāṅgirasa etad itihāsapūrāṇam abhyatapan ।
tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyāṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso ’jāyata ॥

tr.text: Those Mantras of the Atharva-Veda pressed this Itihasa-Purana. From it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour of limbs, alertness of the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य परःकृष्णं रूपम् ॥
iast: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ rūpam ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: It flowed forth; it settled by the side of the sun. Verily, this it is that appears as the deep black hue of the sun.

sa: अथ ये ऽस्योर्ध्वा रश्मयस् ता एवास्योर्ध्वा मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: atha ye ’syordhvā raśmayas tā evāsyordhvā madhunāḍyaḥ ।
words: a flower; blossom; the menstrual flux

tr.text: And its upper rays are its upper honey cells. The secret teachings are the bees. Brahman (Pranava) is the flower. Those waters (the results of the meditations on the Pranava) are the nectar.

sa: ते वा एते गुह्या आदेशा एतद् ब्रह्माभ्यतपन् ।
तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
iast: te vā ete guhyā ādeśā etad brahmābhyatapan ।
tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso ’jāyata ॥

tr.text: Those secret teachings pressed this Pranava. From it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour of limbs, alertness of the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य मध्ये क्षोभत इव ॥
iast: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya madhye kṣobhata iva ॥
words: to flow away or into; to trickle through
to shake; to tremble; to be agitated or disturbed

tr.text: It flowed forth; it settled by the side of the sun. Verily, this it is that appears as the quivering in the middle of the sun.

Verily, these hues are the juice of the juices, for the Vedas are the essences and these are their essence. These hues indeed are the nectar of the nectars, for the Vedas are the nectar and these are their nectar.

sa: तद् यत् प्रथमम् अमृतं तद् वसव उपजीवन्त्य् अग्निना मुखेन ।
न वै देवा अश्नन्ति न पिबन्ति ।
iast: tad yat prathamam amṛtaṃ tad vasava upajīvanty agninā mukhena ।
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti ।

tr.text: That which is the first nectar (i.e. the red form), that verily Vasus enjoy with Agni as their leader. The gods, indeed, neither eat nor drink, only with seeing this nectar are they satisfied.
They enter into this very form (colour) and out of this form they emerge.

sa: स य एतद् एवम् अमृतं वेद वसूनाम् एवैको भूत्वाग्निनैव मुखेनैतद् एवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यति ।
iast: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda vasūnām evaiko bhūtvāgninaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati ।

tr.text: He who knows thus this nectar becomes one of the Vasus, and with Agni as the leader, is satisfied only with seeing this nectar. He enters into this very form and out of this form he emerges.

sa: स यावद् आदित्यः पुरस्ताद् उदेता पश्चाद् अस्तम् एता वसूनाम् एव तावद् आधिपत्यं स्वाराज्यं पर्येता ॥
iast: sa yāvad ādityaḥ purastād udetā paścād astam etā vasūnām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ॥

tr.text: As long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west, so long does he retain the sovereignty and the heavenly kingdom of (or similar to that of) the Vasus.

sa: अथ यद् द्वितीयम् अमृतं तद् रुद्रा उपजीवन्तीन्द्रेण मुखेन ।
न वै देवा अश्नन्ति न पिबन्ति ।
iast: atha yad dvitīyam amṛtaṃ tad rudrā upajīvantīndreṇa mukhena ।
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti ।
words: forming the 2nd part or half of anything
name of the god of tempests and father and ruler of the Rudras and Maruts
the god of the atmosphere and sky

tr.text: And that which is the second nectar (i.e. the white form), that verily the Rudras enjoy with Indra as their leader. The gods, indeed, neither eat nor drink; only with seeing this nectar are they satisfied.

words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: They enter into this very form and out of this form they emerge.

sa: स य एतद् एवम् अमृतं वेद रुद्राणाम् एवैको भूत्वेन्द्रेणैव मुखेनैतद् एवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यति ।
iast: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda rudrāṇām evaiko bhūtvendreṇaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati ।
words: name of the god of tempests and father and ruler of the Rudras and Maruts
the god of the atmosphere and sky
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: He who knows thus this nectar becomes one of the Rudras, and with Indra as the leader, is satisfied only with seeing this nectar. He enters into this very form and out of this form he emerges.

sa: स यावद् आदित्यः पुरस्ताद् उदेता पश्चाद् अस्तम् एता द्विस् तावद् दक्षिणत उदेतोत्तरतो ऽस्तम् एता रुद्राणाम् एव तावद् आधिपत्यं स्वाराज्यं पर्येता ॥
iast: sa yāvad ādityaḥ purastād udetā paścād astam etā dvis tāvad dakṣiṇata udetottarato ’stam etā rudrāṇām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)
name of the god of tempests and father and ruler of the Rudras and Maruts

tr.text: As long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west, even twice so long does he (the Sun) rise in the south and set in the north and even so long does he retain the sovereignty and the heavenly kingdom of the Rudras.

sa: अथ यत् तृतीयम् अमृतं तद् आदित्या उपजीवन्ति वरुणेन मुखेन ।
न वै देवा अश्नन्ति न पिबन्ति ।
iast: atha yat tṛtīyam amṛtaṃ tad ādityā upajīvanti varuṇena mukhena ।
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti ।
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: And that which is the third nectar (i.e. the black form), that verily the Adityas enjoy with Varuna as their leader. The gods, indeed, neither eat nor drink; only with seeing this nectar are they satisfied.

words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: They enter into this very form and out of this form they emerge.

sa: स य एतद् एवम् अमृतं वेदादित्यानाम् एवैको भूत्वा वरुणेनैव मुखेनैतद् एवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यति ।
iast: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ vedādityānām evaiko bhūtvā varuṇenaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati ।
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: He who knows thus this nectar becomes one of the Adityas, and with Varuna as the leader, is satisfied only with seeing this nectar. He enters into this very form and out of this form he emerges.

sa: स यावद् आदित्यो दक्षिणत उदेतोत्तरतो ऽस्तम् एता द्विस् तावत् पश्चाद् उदेता पुरस्ताद् अस्तम् एतादित्यानाम् एव तावद् आधिपत्यं स्वाराज्यं पर्येता ॥
iast: sa yāvad ādityo dakṣiṇata udetottarato ’stam etā dvis tāvat paścād udetā purastād astam etādityānām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)
name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: As long as the sun rises in the south and sets in the north, even twice so long does he (the Sun) rise in the west and set in the east and even so long does he retain the sovereignty and the heavenly kingdom of the Adityas.

sa: अथ यच् चतुर्थम् अमृतं तन् मरुत उपजीवन्ति सोमेन मुखेन ।
न वै देवा अश्नन्ति न पिबन्ति ।
iast: atha yac caturtham amṛtaṃ tan maruta upajīvanti somena mukhena ।
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti ।

tr.text: And that which is the fourth nectar (i.e. the deep black colour), that verily the Maruts enjoy with Soma as their leader. The gods, indeed, neither eat nor drink; only with seeing this nectar are they satisfied.

words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: They enter into this very form and out of this form they emerge.

sa: स य एतद् एवम् अमृतं वेद मरुताम् एवैको भूत्वा सोमेनैव मुखेनैतद् एवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यति ।
iast: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda marutām evaiko bhūtvā somenaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati ।
words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: He who knows thus this nectar becomes one of the Maruts, and with Soma as the leader is satisfied only with seeing this nectar.

sa: स यावद् आदित्यः पश्चाद् उदेता पुरस्ताद् अस्तम् एता द्विस् तावद् उत्तरत उदेता दक्षिणतो ऽस्तम् एता मरुताम् एव तावद् आधिपत्यं स्वाराज्यं पर्येता ॥
iast: sa yāvad ādityaḥ paścād udetā purastād astam etā dvis tāvad uttarata udetā dakṣiṇato ’stam etā marutām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)

tr.text: As long as the sun rises in the west and sets in the east, even twice so long does he (the Sun) rise in the north and set in the south and even so long does he retain the sovereignty and the heavenly kingdom of the Maruts.

sa: अथ यत् पञ्चमम् अमृतं तत् साध्या उपजीवन्ति ब्रह्मणा मुखेन ।
न वै देवा अश्नन्ति न पिबन्ति ।
iast: atha yat pañcamam amṛtaṃ tat sādhyā upajīvanti brahmaṇā mukhena ।
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti ।
words: name of a class of celestial beings (belonging to the gaṇadevatā)

tr.text: And that which is the fifth nectar (i.e. the quivering form within the sun), that verily the Sadhyas enjoy with Pranava as their leader. The gods, indeed, neither eat nor drink; only with seeing this nectar are they satisfied.

words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: They enter into this very form and out of this form they emerge.

sa: स य एतद् एवम् अमृतं वेद साध्यानाम् एवैको भूत्वा ब्रह्मणैव मुखेनैतद् एवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यति ।
iast: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda sādhyānām evaiko bhūtvā brahmaṇaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati ।
words: name of a class of celestial beings (belonging to the gaṇadevatā)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: He who knows thus this nectar becomes one of the Sadhyas, and with Pranava as the leader is satisfied only with seeing this nectar.

sa: स यावद् आदित्य उत्तरत उदेता दक्षिणतो ऽस्तम् एता द्विस् तावद् ऊर्ध्वम् उदेतार्वाग् अस्तम् एता साध्यानाम् एव तावद् आधिपत्यं स्वाराज्यं पर्येता ॥
iast: sa yāvad āditya uttarata udetā dakṣiṇato ’stam etā dvis tāvad ūrdhvam udetārvāg astam etā sādhyānām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)
name of a class of celestial beings (belonging to the gaṇadevatā)

tr.text: As long as the sun rises in the north and sets in the south, even twice so long does he (the Sun) rise in overhead and set below and even so long does he retain the sovereignty and the heavenly kingdom of the Sadhyas.

sa: अथ तत ऊर्ध्व उदेत्य नैवोदेता नास्तम् एतैकल एव मध्ये स्थाता ।
iast: atha tata ūrdhva udetya naivodetā nāstam etaikala eva madhye sthātā ।
words: alone; solitary; (in mus.) a solo singer

tr.text: Then, rising from there upward, he will neither rise nor set. He will remain alone in the middle. There is this verse about it:

words: to hurt; to injure; to lose

tr.text: ‘Never does this happen there. Never did the sun set there nor did it rise. O gods, by this, my assertion of the truth, may I not fall from Brahman’.

sa: न ह वा अस्मा उदेति न निम्लोचति ।
iast: na ha vā asmā udeti na nimlocati ।

tr.text: Verily, for him the sun neither rises nor sets. He who thus knows this secret of the Vedas, for him, there is perpetual day.

sa: तद् धैतद् उद्दालकायारुणये ज्येष्ठाय पुत्राय पिता ब्रह्म प्रोवाच ॥
iast: tad dhaitad uddālakāyāruṇaye jyeṣṭhāya putrāya pitā brahma provāca ॥

tr.text: Hiranyagarbha imparted this Doctrine of Honey to Prajapati, Prajapati to Manu, and Manu to his progeny. And the father told his eldest son Uddalaka Aruni this very knowledge of Brahman.

sa: इदं वाव तज् ज्येष्ठाय पुत्राय पिता ब्रह्म प्रब्रूयात् प्रणाय्याय वान्तेवासिने ॥
iast: idaṃ vāva taj jyeṣṭhāya putrāya pitā brahma prabrūyāt praṇāyyāya vāntevāsine ॥

tr.text: A father may declare to his eldest son or to any other worthy disciple this very knowledge of Honey.

sa: यद्य् अप्य् अस्मा इमाम् अद्भिः परिगृहीतां धनस्य पूर्णां दद्याद् एतद् एव ततो भूय इति ॥
iast: yady apy asmā imām adbhiḥ parigṛhītāṃ dhanasya pūrṇāṃ dadyād etad eva tato bhūya iti ॥
words: to take hold of on both sides; to embrace; to surround

tr.text: And not to any one else, even if one should offer him this sea-girt earth filled with wealth. This (doctrine) is certainly greater than that. This certainly is greater than that.

sa: गायत्री वा इदं सर्वं भूतं यद् इदम् किञ्च ।
वाग् वा इदं सर्वं भूतं गायति च त्रायते च ॥
iast: gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yad idam kiñca ।
vāg vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ gāyati ca trāyate ca ॥

tr.text: Gayatri indeed is all this, whatever being exists. Speech indeed is Gayatri; for speech indeed sings and removes fear of all this that exists.

sa: या वै सा गायत्रीयं वाव सा येयं पृथिवी ।
iast: yā vai sā gāyatrīyaṃ vāva sā yeyaṃ pṛthivī ।
words: to precede in lying down; to surpass; to excel

tr.text: That which is this Gayatri, even that is this earth; for on this earth are all the beings established and they do not transcend it.

sa: या वै सा पृथिवीयं वाव सा यद् इदम् अस्मिन् पुरुषे शरीरम् ।
iast: yā vai sā pṛthivīyaṃ vāva sā yad idam asmin puruṣe śarīram ।
words: to precede in lying down; to surpass; to excel

tr.text: That which is this earth (as Gayatri), even that is this, i.e. this body in respect of this person; for these senses are indeed established in this body and they do not transcend it.

sa: यद् वै तत् पुरुषे शरीरम् इदं वाव तद् यद् इदम् अस्मिन्न् अन्तः पुरुषे हृदयम् ।
iast: yad vai tat puruṣe śarīram idaṃ vāva tad yad idam asminn antaḥ puruṣe hṛdayam ।
words: to precede in lying down; to surpass; to excel

tr.text: That which is the body in respect of a person, even that is identical with) the heart within this body; for these senses are indeed established in it and they do not transcend it.

words: to declare or state or utter with reference to (acc.); to declare; to declare as a verse

tr.text: This well-known Gayatri is four footed and sixfold. The Gayatri Brahman is thus expressed in the following Rik:

sa: तावान् अस्य महिमा ततो ज्यायांश् च पुरुषः ।
पादो ऽस्य सर्वा भूतानि त्रिपाद् अस्यामृतं दिवीति ॥
iast: tāvān asya mahimā tato jyāyāṃś ca puruṣaḥ ।
pādo ’sya sarvā bhūtāni tripād asyāmṛtaṃ divīti ॥

tr.text: Such is the greatness of this (Brahman called Gayatri). The Person is even greater than this. All this world is a quarter of Him, the other three quarters of His constitute immortality in heaven.

sa: यद् वै तद् ब्रह्मेतीदं वाव तद् यो ऽयं बहिर्धा पुरुषाद् आकाशः ।
यो वै स बहिर्धा पुरुषाद् आकाशः ॥
iast: yad vai tad brahmetīdaṃ vāva tad yo ’yaṃ bahirdhā puruṣād ākāśaḥ ।
yo vai sa bahirdhā puruṣād ākāśaḥ ॥
words: out; outward; outside of or away from (abl.)
out; outward; outside of or away from (abl.)

tr.text: That which is (designated as) Brahman, even that is this Akasa outside the body. That which is the Akasa outside the body, even that is the Akasa inside the body. That which is the Akasa inside the body, even that is this Akasa within the (lotus of the) heart. This Brahman is all-filling and unchanging. He who knows (Brahman) thus, gets all-filling and unchanging prosperity.

sa: अयं वाव स यो ऽयम् अन्तः पुरुष आकाशः ।
यो वै सो ऽन्तः पुरुष आकाशः ॥
iast: ayaṃ vāva sa yo ’yam antaḥ puruṣa ākāśaḥ ।

tr.text: That which is (designated as) Brahman, even that is this Akasa outside the body. That which is the Akasa outside the body, even that is the Akasa inside the body. That which is the Akasa inside the body, even that is this Akasa within the (lotus of the) heart. This Brahman is all-filling and unchanging. He who knows (Brahman) thus, gets all-filling and unchanging prosperity.

sa: अयं वाव स यो ऽयम् अन्तर्हृदय आकाशः ।
पूर्णम् अप्रवर्तिनीं श्रियं लभते य एवं वेद ॥
iast: ayaṃ vāva sa yo ’yam antarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ ।
pūrṇam apravartinīṃ śriyaṃ labhate ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: That which is (designated as) Brahman, even that is this Akasa outside the body. That which is the Akasa outside the body, even that is the Akasa inside the body. That which is the Akasa inside the body, even that is this Akasa within the (lotus of the) heart. This Brahman is all-filling and unchanging. He who knows (Brahman) thus, gets all-filling and unchanging prosperity.

sa: तस्य ह वा एतस्य हृदयस्य पञ्च देवसुषयः ।
स यो ऽस्य प्राङ् सुषिः स प्राणः ।
तद् एतत् तेजो ऽन्नाद्यम् इत्य् उपासीत ।
तेजस्व्य् अन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: tasya ha vā etasya hṛdayasya pañca devasuṣayaḥ ।
sa yo ’sya prāṅ suṣiḥ sa prāṇaḥ ।
tejasvy annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: Of the said heart, there are, indeed, five doors guarded by the gods. (He who is in) that which is the eastern door of this, is Prana. He is the eye, he is the sun. This (Brahman called Prana) should be meditated upon as brightness and as the source of food. He who meditates thus, becomes resplendent and an eater of food.

sa: अथ यो ऽस्य दक्षिणः सुषिः स व्यानः ।
तद् एतच् छ्रीश् च यशश् चेत्य् उपासीत ।
श्रीमान् यशस्वी भवति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: atha yo ’sya dakṣiṇaḥ suṣiḥ sa vyānaḥ ।
tad etac chrīś ca yaśaś cety upāsīta ।
śrīmān yaśasvī bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: And (he who is in) that which is the southern door of this (heart), is Vyana. He is the ear, he is the moon. This (Brahman called Vyana) should be meditated upon as prosperity and fame. He who meditates thus becomes prosperous and famous.

sa: अथ यो ऽस्य प्रत्यङ् सुषिः सो ऽपानः ।
तद् एतद् ब्रह्मवर्चसम् अन्नाद्यम् इत्य् उपासीत ।
ब्रह्मवर्चस्य् अन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: tad etad brahmavarcasam annādyam ity upāsīta ।
brahmavarcasy annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: And (he who is in) that which is the western door of this (heart), is Apana. He is speech, he is fire. This (Brahman called Apana) should be meditated upon as the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom and as the source of food. He who meditates thus becomes radiant with the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom and also an eater of food.

sa: अथ यो ऽस्योदङ् सुषिः स समानः ।
तद् एतत् कीर्तिश् च व्युष्टिश् चेत्युपासीत ।
कीर्तिमान् व्युष्टिमान् भवति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: tad etat kīrtiś ca vyuṣṭiś cetyupāsīta ।
kīrtimān vyuṣṭimān bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥
words: the first gleam or breaking of dawn; daybreak; consequence

tr.text: And (he who is in) that which is the northern door of this (heart), is Samana. He is the mind, he is Parjanya (the rain-god). This (Brahman called Samana) should be meditated upon as fame and grace. He who meditates thus becomes famous and graceful.

sa: अथ यो ऽस्योर्ध्वः सुषिः स उदानः ।
तद् एतद् ओजश् च महश् चेत्य् उपासीत ।
ओजस्वी महस्वान् भवति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: tad etad ojaś ca mahaś cety upāsīta ।
ojasvī mahasvān bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: And (he who is in) that which is the upper door of this (heart), is Udana. He is the air, he is the Akasa. This (Brahman called Udana) should be meditated upon as strength and nobility. He who meditates thus becomes strong and noble.

sa: ते वा एते पञ्च ब्रह्मपुरुषाः स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपाः ।
स य एतान् एवं पञ्च ब्रह्मपुरुषान् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपान् वेदास्य कुले वीरो जायते ।
प्रतिपद्यते स्वर्गं लोकं य एतान् एवं पञ्च ब्रह्मपुरुषान् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपान् वेद ॥
iast: te vā ete pañca brahmapuruṣāḥ svargasya lokasya dvārapāḥ ।
sa ya etān evaṃ pañca brahmapuruṣān svargasya lokasya dvārapān vedāsya kule vīro jāyate ।
pratipadyate svargaṃ lokaṃ ya etān evaṃ pañca brahmapuruṣān svargasya lokasya dvārapān veda ॥

tr.text: These, verily, are the five persons under Brahman, the sentinels of the heavenly world. He who adores thus these five persons under Brahman, the sentinels of the heavenly world, in his family is a hero born. He who adores thus these five persons under Brahman, the sentinels of the heavenly world, reaches the heavenly world.

sa: अथ यद् अतः परो दिवो ज्योतिर् दीप्यते विश्वतःपृष्ठेषु सर्वतःपृष्ठेष्व् अनुत्तमेषूत्तमेषु लोकेष्व् इदं वाव तद् यद् इदम् अस्मिन्न् अन्तः पुरुषे ज्योतिः । ॥
iast: atha yad ataḥ paro divo jyotir dīpyate viśvataḥpṛṣṭheṣu sarvataḥpṛṣṭheṣv anuttameṣūttameṣu lokeṣv idaṃ vāva tad yad idam asminn antaḥ puruṣe jyotiḥ । ॥
words: unsurpassed; incomparably the best or chief; excellent

tr.text: Again, the light of Brahman that shines above this heaven, above everything, above all, in the incomparably good and the highest worlds, even this is the light within the body of man. This light can be seen inasmuch as one has a perception of warmth when one touches the body. It can be heard inasmuch as, on closing the ears, one hears something like the sound of a chariot or the bellowing of a bull, or the sound of a blazing fire. One should meditate on the light as seen and heard. One who meditates on this thus, becomes beautiful and illustrious – yea, one who meditates thus.

sa: तस्यैषा दृष्टिर् यत्रैतद् अस्मिञ् छरीरे संस्पर्शेनोष्णिमानं विजानाति ।
तस्यैषा श्रुतिर् यत्रैतत् कर्णाव् अपिगृह्य निनदम् इव नदथुर् इवाग्नेर् इव ज्वलत उपशृनोति ।
तद् एतद् दृष्टं च श्रुतं चेत्य् उपासीत ।
चक्षुष्यः श्रुतो भवति य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
iast: tasyaiṣā dṛṣṭir yatraitad asmiñ charīre saṃsparśenoṣṇimānaṃ vijānāti ।
tasyaiṣā śrutir yatraitat karṇāv apigṛhya ninadam iva nadathur ivāgner iva jvalata upaśṛnoti ।
tad etad dṛṣṭaṃ ca śrutaṃ cety upāsīta ।
cakṣuṣyaḥ śruto bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ॥
words: close or mutual contact; touch; conjunction
close or mutual contact; touch; conjunction
to burn brightly; to blaze; to glow
pleasing to the eyes; wholesome for the eyes or the eyesight; agreeable to the eyes

tr.text: There is this seeing of it— when one perceives by touch this heat here in the body. There is this hearing of it— when one closes his ears and hears as it were a sound, as it were a noise, as of a fire blazing. One should reverence that light as something that has been seen and heard. He becomes one beautiful to see, one heard of in renown, who knows this — yea, who knows this!

sa: सर्वं खल्व् इदं ब्रह्म तज्जलान् इति शान्त उपासीत ।
अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुर् अस्मिंल् लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति ।
iast: sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma tajjalān iti śānta upāsīta ।
atha khalu kratumayaḥ puruṣo yathākratur asmiṃl loke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati ।
words: water; any fluid; a kind of Andropogon

tr.text: Verily, all this universe is Brahman. From Him do all things originate, into Him do they dissolve and by Him are they sustained. On Him should one meditate in tranquillity. For as is one’s faith, such indeed one is; and as is one’s faith in this world, such one becomes on departing hence. Let one, therefore, cultivate faith.

sa: मनोमयः प्राणशरीरो भारूपः सत्यसंकल्प आकाशात्मा सर्वकर्मा सर्वकामः सर्वगन्धः सर्वरसः सर्वम् इदम् अभ्यत्तो ऽवाक्य् अनादरः ॥
iast: manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīro bhārūpaḥ satyasaṃkalpa ākāśātmā sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ sarvam idam abhyatto ’vāky anādaraḥ ॥
words: to seize; to snatch away; to take up the word

tr.text: He, who is permeating the mind, who has Prana for his body, whose nature is consciousness, whose resolve is infallible, whose own form is like Akasa, whose creation is all that exists, whose are all the pure desires, who possesses all the agreeable odours and all the pleasant tastes, who exists pervading all this, who is without speech (and other senses), who is free from agitation and eagerness – this my Atman, residing in (the lotus of) the heart – is smaller than a grain of paddy, than a barley corn, than a mustard seed, than a grain of millet or than the kernel of a grain of millet. This my Atman residing in (the lotus of) the heart is greater than the earth, greater than the sky, greater than heaven, greater than all these worlds.

sa: एष म आत्मा अन्तर्हृदये ऽणीयान् व्रीहेर् वा यवाद् वा सर्षपाद् वा श्यामाकाद् वा श्यामाकतण्डुलाद् वा ।
एष म आत्मा अन्तर्हृदये ज्यायान् पृथिव्या ज्यायान् अन्तरिक्षाज् ज्यायान् दिवो ज्यायान् एभ्यो लोकेभ्यः ॥
iast: eṣa ma ātmā antarhṛdaye ’ṇīyān vrīher vā yavād vā sarṣapād vā śyāmākād vā śyāmākataṇḍulād vā ।
eṣa ma ātmā antarhṛdaye jyāyān pṛthivyā jyāyān antarikṣāj jyāyān divo jyāyān ebhyo lokebhyaḥ ॥
words: Panicum Frumentaceum; name of a man; name of a people
Panicum Frumentaceum; name of a man; name of a people
grain (after threshing and winnowing); rice; rice used as a weight

tr.text: He, who is permeating the mind, who has Prana for his body, whose nature is consciousness, whose resolve is infallible, whose own form is like Akasa, whose creation is all that exists, whose are all the pure desires, who possesses all the agreeable odours and all the pleasant tastes, who exists pervading all this, who is without speech (and other senses), who is free from agitation and eagerness – this my Atman, residing in (the lotus of) the heart – is smaller than a grain of paddy, than a barley corn, than a mustard seed, than a grain of millet or than the kernel of a grain of millet. This my Atman residing in (the lotus of) the heart is greater than the earth, greater than the sky, greater than heaven, greater than all these worlds.

sa: सर्वकर्मा सर्वकामः सर्वगन्धः सर्वरसः सर्वम् इदम् अभ्यत्तो ऽवाक्यनादरः ।
एतम् इतः प्रेत्याभिसंभविता अस्मीति यस्य स्याद् अद्धा न विचिकित्सा अस्ति ।
iast: sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ sarvam idam abhyatto ’vākyanādaraḥ ।
etam itaḥ pretyābhisaṃbhavitā asmīti yasya syād addhā na vicikitsā asti ।
words: to seize; to snatch away; to take up the word

tr.text: He, whose creation is all that exists, whose are all the pure desires, who possesses all the agreeable odours and all the pleasant tastes, who exists pervading all this, who is without speech (and other senses), who is free from agitation and eagerness, He is my Atman residing in (the lotus of) the heart; He is Brahman. On departing hence I shall attain to His being. He alone who possesses this faith and has no doubt about it (will obtain the result). Thus declared Sandilya – yea, Sandilya.

sa: दिशो ह्य् अस्य स्रक्तयो द्यौर् अस्योत्तरं बिलम् ।
स एष कोशो वसुधानस् तस्मिन् विश्वम् इदं श्रितम् ॥
iast: diśo hy asya sraktayo dyaur asyottaraṃ bilam ।
sa eṣa kośo vasudhānas tasmin viśvam idaṃ śritam ॥
words: the intermediate space between heaven and earth

tr.text: The chest (i.e. the universe), having the sky as its hollow and the earth for its (curved) bottom, does not decay. The quarters are indeed its corners and heaven its upper lid. This well-known chest is the container of wealth. All things rest in it.

sa: स य एतम् एवं वायुं दिशां वत्सं वेद न पुत्ररोदं रोदिति ।
सो ऽहम् एतम् एवं वायुं दिशां वत्सं वेद ।
iast: sa ya etam evaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda na putrarodaṃ roditi ।
so ’ham etam evaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda ।

tr.text: Of that chest, the eastern quarter is named Juhu, the southern is named Sahamana, the western is named Rajni and the northern is named Subhuta. The air is their calf. He who knows this air, the calf of the quarters, thus (as immortal), never weeps in mourning for his son. I, wishing my son’s, longevity, worship thus this air, the calf of the quarters. May I never weep to mourn my son.

tr.text: I take refuge in the imperishable chest for such and such and such. I take refuge in Prana for such and such and such. I take refuge in Bhuh for such and such and such. I take refuge in Bhuvah for such and such and such. I take refuge in Svah for such and such and such.

sa: स यद् अवोचं प्राणं प्रपद्य इति ।
प्रानो वा इदं सर्वं भूतं यद् इदं किंच ।
iast: sa yad avocaṃ prāṇaṃ prapadya iti ।
prāno vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca ।
words: to fall or drop down from (abl.)

tr.text: When I said, ‘I take refuge in Prana’, (it was because) all these beings, whatsoever exist, are indeed Prana. So it was in this alone that I took refuge.

sa: अथ यदवोचं भूः प्रपद्य इति पृथिवीं प्रपद्येऽन्तरिक्षं
iast: atha yadavocaṃ bhūḥ prapadya iti pṛthivīṃ prapadye’ntarikṣaṃ

tr.text: Then when I said, ‘I take refuge in Bhuh’, I said only this: ‘I take refuge in the earth, I take refuge in the sky, I take refuge in heaven’.

sa: अथ यद् अवोचं भुवः प्रपद्य इत्य् अग्निं प्रपद्ये वायुं प्रपद्य आदित्यं प्रपद्य इत्य् एव तद् अवोचम् ॥
iast: atha yad avocaṃ bhuvaḥ prapadya ity agniṃ prapadye vāyuṃ prapadya ādityaṃ prapadya ity eva tad avocam ॥

tr.text: Then when I said, ‘I take refuge in Bhuvah’, I said only this: ‘I take refuge in Fire, I take refuge in Air, I take refuge in the Sun.’

sa: अथ यद् अवोचं स्वः प्रपद्य इत्य् ऋग्वेदं प्रपद्ये यजुर्वेदं प्रपद्ये सामवेदं प्रपद्य इत्य् एव तद् अवोचम् ॥
iast: atha yad avocaṃ svaḥ prapadya ity ṛgvedaṃ prapadye yajurvedaṃ prapadye sāmavedaṃ prapadya ity eva tad avocam ॥

tr.text: Then, when I said, ‘I take refuge in Svah’, I said only this: ‘I take refuge in the Rig-Veda, I take refuge in the Yajur-Veda, I take refuge in the Sama-Veda’ – yea, that was what I said.

words: an ancient metre of twentyfour syllables

tr.text: Man, truly, is the sacrifice. His (first) twenty-four years are the morning libation, for the metre Gayatri is made up of twenty-four syllables, and the morning libation is related to the Gayatri metre. With this the Vasus are connected. The Pranas indeed are the Vasus, for they make all this stable.

sa: तं चेद् एतस्मिन् वयसि किंचिद् उपतपेत् स ब्रूयात् ।
प्राणा वसव इदं मे प्रातःसवनं माध्यंदिनं सवनम् अनुसंतनुतेति माहं प्राणानां वसूनां मध्ये यज्ञो विलोप्सीयेति ।
उद् धैव तत एत्य् अगदो ह भवति ॥
iast: taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt ।
prāṇā vasava idaṃ me prātaḥsavanaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānāṃ vasūnāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti ।
ud dhaiva tata ety agado ha bhavati ॥
words: the act of pressing out the Soma-juice (performed at the three periods of the da

tr.text: During this period of life if anything (e.g. illness) causes him pain, he should repeat: ‘O Pranas, Vasus, unite this morning libation of mind with the midday libation. May I who am a sacrifice not be lost in the midst of the Vasus who are the Pranas’. He surely recovers from that and becomes healthy.

sa: अथ यानि चतुश्चत्वारिंशद् वर्षाणि तन् माध्यंदिनं सवनम् ।
iast: atha yāni catuścatvāriṃśad varṣāṇi tan mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam ।
words: the act of pressing out the Soma-juice (performed at the three periods of the da
the act of pressing out the Soma-juice (performed at the three periods of the da

tr.text: Now, (his next) forty-four years are the mid-day libation, (for) the metre Tristubh is made up of forty-four syllables, and the mid-day libation is related to the Tristubh metre. With this, the Rudras are connected. The Pranas indeed are the Rudras, for they cause all this (universe) to weep.

sa: तं चेद् एतस्मिन् वयसि किंचिद् उपतपेत् स ब्रूयात् ।
प्राणा रुद्रा इदं मे माध्यंदिनं सवनं तृतीयसवनम् अनुसंतनुतेति माहं प्राणानां रुद्राणां मध्ये यज्ञो विलोप्सीयेति ।
उद् धैव तत एत्य् अगदो ह भवति ॥
iast: taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt ।
prāṇā rudrā idaṃ me mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ tṛtīyasavanam anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti ।
ud dhaiva tata ety agado ha bhavati ॥
words: name of the god of tempests and father and ruler of the Rudras and Maruts
the act of pressing out the Soma-juice (performed at the three periods of the da
name of the god of tempests and father and ruler of the Rudras and Maruts

tr.text: During this period of life if anything (e.g. illness) causes him pain, he should repeat: ‘O Pranas, Rudras, unite this mid-day libation of mine with the third libation. May I, who am a sacrifice, not be lost in the midst of the Rudras who are the Pranas’. He surely recovers from that and becomes healthy.

sa: अथ यान्य् अष्टाचत्वारिंशद् वर्षाणि तत् तृतीयसवनम् ।
iast: atha yāny aṣṭācatvāriṃśad varṣāṇi tat tṛtīyasavanam ।

tr.text: Then (his next) forty-eight years are the third libation. The metre Jagati is made up of fortyeight syllables and the third libation is related to the Jagati metre. With this, the Adityas are connected. The Pranas indeed are the Adityas, for they accept all this.

sa: तं चेद् एतस्मिन् वयसि किंचिद् उपतपेत् स ब्रूयात् ।
प्राणा आदित्या इदं मे तृतीयसवनम् आयुर् अनुसंतनुतेति माहं प्राणानाम् आदित्यानां मध्ये यज्ञो विलोप्सीयेति ।
उद् धैव तत एत्य् अगदो हैव भवति ॥
iast: taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt ।
prāṇā ādityā idaṃ me tṛtīyasavanam āyur anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānām ādityānāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti ।
ud dhaiva tata ety agado haiva bhavati ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: During this period of life if anything (e.g. illness) causes him pain, he should repeat: ‘O Pranas, Adityas, extend this third libation of mine to a full length of life. May I, who am a sacrifice, not be lost in the midst of the Adityas who are the Pranas.’ He surely recovers from that and becomes healthy.

sa: एतद् ध स्म वै तद् विद्वान् आह महिदास ऐतरेयः ।
स किं म एतद् उपतपसि यो ऽहम् अनेन न प्रेष्याम् इति ।
प्र ह षोडशं वर्षशतं जीवति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: etad dha sma vai tad vidvān āha mahidāsa aitareyaḥ ।
sa kiṃ ma etad upatapasi yo ’ham anena na preṣyām iti ।
pra ha ṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśataṃ jīvati ya evaṃ veda ॥
words: name of a son of Itarā
a descendant of Itara or Itarā

tr.text: Knowing this well-known (doctrine of sacrifice) Aitareya Mahidasa said, ‘Why do you afflict me thus, me who cannot be so killed.’ He lived for one hundred and sixteen years. He, too, who knows thus, lives in vigour for one hundred and sixteen years.

sa: स यद् अशिशिषति यत् पिपासति यन् न रमते ता अस्य दीक्षाः ॥
iast: sa yad aśiśiṣati yat pipāsati yan na ramate tā asya dīkṣāḥ ॥
words: preparation or consecration for a religious ceremony

tr.text: That he (who performs the Purusha sacrifice) feels hunger, that he feels thirst, that he does not rejoice –all these are the initiatory rites of this sacrifice.

sa: अथ यद् अश्नाति यत् पिबति यद् रमते तद् उपसदैर् एति ॥
iast: atha yad aśnāti yat pibati yad ramate tad upasadair eti ॥

tr.text: And, that he eats that he drinks, that he rejoices – all these approach Upasadas.

sa: अथ यद् धसति यज् जक्षति यन् मैथुनं चरति स्तुतशस्त्रैर् एव तद् एति ॥
iast: atha yad dhasati yaj jakṣati yan maithunaṃ carati stutaśastrair eva tad eti ॥
words: an instrument for cutting or wounding

tr.text: And, that he laughs, that he eats, that he behaves as one of a couple – all these approach Stotra and Sastra.

sa: अथ यत् तपो दानम् आर्जवम् अहिंसा सत्यवचनम् इति ता अस्य दक्षिणाः ॥
iast: atha yat tapo dānam ārjavam ahiṃsā satyavacanam iti tā asya dakṣiṇāḥ ॥

tr.text: And his austerity, gifts, uprightness, non-violence, and truthfulness – all these are the largesses of this sacrifice.
Therefore people say ‘sosyati’ (will procreate), and ‘asosta’ (has procreated). Again, that is the procreation of this, and death is the Avabhrita bath.

sa: तद् धैतद् घोर आङ्गिरसः कृष्णाय देवकीपुत्रायोक्त्वोवाच ।
सो ऽन्तवेलायाम् एतत् त्रयं प्रतिपद्येताक्षितम् अस्य् अच्युतम् असि प्राणसंशितम् असीति ।
iast: tad dhaitad ghora āṅgirasaḥ kṛṣṇāya devakīputrāyoktvovāca ।
so ’ntavelāyām etat trayaṃ pratipadyetākṣitam asy acyutam asi prāṇasaṃśitam asīti ।
words: the dark half of the lunar month from full to new moon
name of a daughter of Devaka who was wife of Vasudeva and mother of Kṛṣṇa (ident

tr.text: Ghora Angirasa expounded this well-known doctrine to Devaki’s son Krishna and said, ‘Such a knower should, at the time of death, repeat this triad – "Thou art the imperishable, Thou art unchangeable, Thou art the subtle essence of Prana". (On hearing the above) he became thirstless. There are these two Rik stanzas in regard to this.

sa: देवं देवत्रा सूर्यम् अगन्म ज्योतिर् उत्तमम् इति ज्योतिर् उत्तमम् इति ॥
iast: devaṃ devatrā sūryam aganma jyotir uttamam iti jyotir uttamam iti ॥

tr.text: (Those knowers of Brahman who have purified their mind through the withdrawal of the senses and other means like Brahmacharya) see everywhere (the day – like the supreme light) of the ancient One who is the seed of the universe, (the light that shines in the Effulgent Brahman). May we, too having perceived the highest light which dispels darkness, reach it. Having perceived the highest light in our own heart we have reached that highest light, which is the dispeller (of water, rays of light and the Pranas), shining in all gods – yea, we have reached that highest light.

sa: इत्य् उभयम् आदिष्टं भवत्य् अध्यात्मं चाधिदैवतं च ॥
iast: ity ubhayam ādiṣṭaṃ bhavaty adhyātmaṃ cādhidaivataṃ ca ॥

tr.text: The mind is Brahman, thus one should meditate – this is (the meditation) with regard to the body (including the mind). Next, the meditation with regard to the gods – the Akasa is Brahman, thus (one should meditate). Both the meditations, with regard to the body and with regard to the gods are being enjoined.

sa: वाक् पादः प्राणः पादश् चक्षुः पादः श्रोत्रं पादः ।
अग्निः पादो वायुः पाद आदित्यः पादो दिशः पादः ।
इत्य् उभयम् एवादिष्टं भवत्य् अध्यात्मं चाधिदैवतं च ॥
iast: vāk pādaḥ prāṇaḥ pādaś cakṣuḥ pādaḥ śrotraṃ pādaḥ ।
agniḥ pādo vāyuḥ pāda ādityaḥ pādo diśaḥ pādaḥ ।
ity ubhayam evādiṣṭaṃ bhavaty adhyātmaṃ cādhidaivataṃ ca ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: This same Brahman has four feet. The organ of speech is one foot. Prana (the organ of smell) is one foot, the eye is one foot and the ear is one foot. This is with reference to the body. Next, with reference to the gods. Agni is one foot, Vayu is one foot, Aditya is one foot and the quarters are one foot. Thus both the meditations, with reference to the body and with reference to the gods, are enjoined.

sa: सो ऽग्निना ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च ।
भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद ॥
iast: so ’gninā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca ।
bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: The organ of speech is one of the four feet of Brahman (called Mind). With the light of fire it shines and warms. He who knows thus, shines and warms with fame and celebrity and with the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom.

sa: स वायुना ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च ।
भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद ॥
iast: sa vāyunā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca ।
bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: The organ of smell is one of the four feet of Brahman. With the light of air it shines and warms. He who knows thus, shines and warms with fame and celebrity and with the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom.

sa: स आदित्येन ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च ।
भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद ॥
iast: sa ādityena jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca ।
bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: The eye is one of the four feet of Brahman. With the light of the sun it shines and warms. He who knows thus, shines and warms with fame and celebrity and with the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom.

sa: स दिग्भिर् ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च ।
भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
iast: sa digbhir jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca ।
bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: The ear is one of the four feet of Brahman. With the light of the quarters it shines and warms. He who knows thus, shines and warms with fame and celebrity and with the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom – yea, he who knows thus.

sa: ते आण्डकपाले रजतं च सुवर्णं चाभवताम् ॥
iast: te āṇḍakapāle rajataṃ ca suvarṇaṃ cābhavatām ॥

tr.text: The Sun is Brahman – this is the teaching. The further explanation of this (is here given). Before creation, this universe was non-existent. Then it became existent. It grew; it turned into an egg; it lay for a period of one year; (and then) it burst open. Of the two halves of that egg-shell, one was of silver and the other of gold.

Of these, that which was of silver is this earth. That which was of gold is heaven. That which was the outer membrane is the mountains. That which was the inner membrane is the mist together with the clouds. Those which were the veins are the rivers. That which was the water in the lower belly is the ocean.

sa: अथ यत् तद् अजायत सो ऽसाव् आदित्यः ।
तं जायमानं घोषा उलूलवो ऽनूदतिष्ठन्त् सर्वाणि च भूतानि सर्वे च कामाः ।
तस्मात् तस्योदयं प्रति प्रत्यायनं प्रति घोषा उलूलवो ऽनूत्तिष्ठन्ति सर्वाणि च भूतानि सर्वे च कामाः ॥
iast: atha yat tad ajāyata so ’sāv ādityaḥ ।
taṃ jāyamānaṃ ghoṣā ulūlavo ’nūdatiṣṭhant sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāḥ ।
tasmāt tasyodayaṃ prati pratyāyanaṃ prati ghoṣā ulūlavo ’nūttiṣṭhanti sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāḥ ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: And that which was born is the yonder sun. After he was born, sounds of the form of loud shouts arose, as also all beings and all desired objects. Therefore at his rise and his every return (or his setting), sounds of the form of loud shouts arise, as also all beings and all desired objects.

sa: स य एतम् एवं विद्वान् आदित्यं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते ।
अभ्याशो ह यद् एनं साधवो घोषा आ च गच्छेयुर् उप च निम्रेडेरन् निम्रेडेरन् ॥
iast: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān ādityaṃ brahmety upāste ।
abhyāśo ha yad enaṃ sādhavo ghoṣā ā ca gaccheyur upa ca nimreḍeran nimreḍeran ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: He who knows the Sun thus and meditates on it as Brahman, auspicious sounds will hasten to him and continue to delight him – yea, will continue to delight.
